scenes.text: You press the power button on a Linux server. What actually happens next?
First, the firmware, UEFI, wakes up. It checks the hardware, then looks for a disk it can boot from.
It hands over to GRUB, the bootloader. GRUB picks which kernel to start.
The kernel loads its drivers, then mounts the real root file system.
Now the kernel starts one process: systemd, P I D one. systemd brings up every service, the network, S S H, your web server, in parallel.
And finally, the login prompt. You're in.
So: firmware, GRUB, kernel, systemd, login.
Interview trap. What is P I D one? Not the kernel. It's systemd.
